title: Ex-OpenAI Safety Leader Says Sam Altman-Led AI Giant Warned About AI Risks While 'Still Training and Depl
key_facts: David Robinson, formerly a leader on OpenAI's Safety Systems team, spoke to Ezra Klein of The New York Times about leaving OpenAI.
He said the 'fundamental cognitive dissonance' was that OpenAI keeps publishing warnings while still training and deploying the dangerous models it warns about.
He described OpenAI's offices as 'frenetic', with people 'running on fumes'.
In September Sam Altman said 'We need to pace the frontier' after agreeing with Dario Amodei's essay on a coordinated slowdown.
OpenAI did not immediately comment; a spokesperson earlier answered Robinson's Atlantic essay saying the company pauses training or holds back models when it needs to slow down.
quote_evidence: "Part of what was the fundamental cognitive dissonance for me was we keep publishing these warnings, but ultimately, we're still training and deploying these dangerous models that we're warning about," Robinson said.
Within OpenAI's office, though, Robinson told Klein that there was continued "frenetic" activity and that people were "running on fumes."
We're making sure our models don't become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down.
why_it_matters_hint: A former safety leader says OpenAI's public warnings and its pace of development do not match.
event_date: Interview date not stated; reported 8 Oct 2026
notes: Benzinga original returned a Cloudflare block; read Business Insider and People Matters Global. Interview date not given.
